packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 01 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING

EXPOSURE / PROCESS NOTES
- Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading of this text before I read it. Two things in context are worth naming: (a) the packet path ("stams4") and pencil shelfmarks written on the objects themselves (image-004 top margin: "Stams, StA, Frg. 236-1r"; image-026 foot: "Stams, StA, Frg. 236-1v"; image-032 left margin: "Stams, StA, Frg. 236-2r"; image-025, blue ink: "aus Hs 287"). These are on the leaf, not proposals. (b) The printed title on the recto ("Inhalt der Tirolischen Landtafel", see below) is visible content. Neither identifies the Latin offset text on the verso.
- Beyond the rules: I made horizontally mirrored copies of verso tiles 015, 016, 017, 019, 020, 022 and 024 (in my session scratchpad, not in the packet) because the verso text is offset, i.e. mirror-reversed. I viewed the mirrored copies of 019, 020, 022 and 024. No other files or directories were opened.
- Image load: images 001-013 and 015-033 first came back "[media removed: request limit]". I reopened all of them except 019, 020, 022 and 024, where I viewed only the mirrored copies (the 019 and 020 originals did display once after removal). Every image in the packet was seen at least once (or, for 022 and 024, as a mirrored copy). No image failed for good.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
The packet covers three faces of two paper fragments:
- Face A = image-001 (overview) with tiles 002-013: the recto of fragment 1. It is not a manuscript text page. It is an engraved (intaglio-hatched) pictorial map in landscape, with place-names in German cursive and Fraktur. A graduated border scale on the right is numbered 30, 35(?), 44(?), 48, 54(?) (the digits are partly mirrored or unclear). The lower right holds the Carinthian-style arms (three lions on the dexter half, crossed/blocked fields on the sinister), a cartouche, and a framed table of contents.
- Face B = image-014 (overview) with tiles 015-026: the verso of fragment 1. This is blank paper carrying OFFSET (mirror-image, brown) transfer of a gothic (textura) Latin text in two columns, apparently from a facing printed or written leaf. A vertical fold or guard strip runs down the centre. There are two blocks of offset: left (about 2 columns) and right (about 2 columns, much fainter). Faint ghosting of the map shows through. No rubrics are directly visible; a few larger initials appear in the offset. Near the right block, image-021 and image-025 show faint reddish traces that might be offset rubrication (tentative).
- Face C = image-027 (overview) with tiles 028-035: the recto of fragment 2. It is a second, damaged copy (or another state) of the same lower-right map area. It shows the same cartouche and table, plus a winged-lion vignette with an open book, and a second cartouche at the lower left.

SELECTED SPANS
1. The engraved table of contents (faces A and C), which is complete enough to transcribe.
2. The cartouches and the vignette book (face C).
3. Representative map labels (face A); this is a sample, not exhaustive.
4. The best-preserved offset Latin, left block of face B, read from mirrored tiles 020, 019, 022 and 024. This is very weak evidence.
Unread or skipped: most of the faint right-hand offset block on face B (tiles 017, 018, 021, 023, 025, 026). It is too faint for connected reading; only isolated letter shapes show.

Cross-check with image-035 (face A right edge, which overlaps image-012): "...ohe Stifft / Stätt / ...märckht. / ...eülsche Heüser sampt der / ...andt Comenterey / ...löster / ...farren / ...irchen. / ...chl[hole]r und Sitz. / ...dörffer. / ...wasserfluss." The image-027 overview reads line 10 as "3?5 Schlösser und Sitz." ("Schl" visible, then a hole, then "und Sitz.").
Hence the probable full line is "[3?5] Schl[össer] vnd Sitz." The middle of it is supplied from overlapping views; the letters themselves are damaged.

--- 4. OFFSET LATIN, FACE B (read reversed; extremely tentative) ---
Physical layout: two columns of textura on the left half of image-014 and two fainter columns on the right half. Readings come from mirrored copies; line numbers are counted from the top of each mirrored tile (left-right is flipped, so the column order is as the original text would read).

Assessment: these "words" are near-guesses from smudged reversed offset. They should not be used for source matching without a much better image (raking or transmitted light, or the facing leaf itself, possibly the "Hs 287" noted on the verso).

LIMITATIONS
- The recto text is a printed/engraved map, not a manuscript; the readings above are of engraved lettering. Abbreviation marks were kept where visible.
- The verso text is offset only (mirror-reversed, partial, faint). The columns are not clearly separable at the gutter, and the vertical fold/guard covers part of the left block's inner margin.
- Fragment 2 (face C) has a torn top edge and holes through the table numerals and the "Schl..." line. The numeral before "Schl" is not secure.
- Suggested follow-up: a higher-contrast or transmitted-light capture of face B; image the facing leaf (the source of the offset) directly.
